newsitem.title: USA: Calif. may be breaking law to pay workers - paper.
newsitem.headline: Calif. may be breaking law to pay workers - paper.

text.p: California may be paying as many as 250,000 workers in violation of state law during its budget impasse, the Los Angeles Times reported Thursday.
California's controller has been paying many state bills without the required legislative authorization, according to the Times, which cited a provision of the state Constitution.
"Money may be drawn from the treasury only through an appropriation made by the law," the provision states.

Since California has been operating without a budget for weeks, the state legislature has made no "appropriation" authorizing the state controller to pay the state's bills, including checks to state workers, the Times said.
Lawmakers continue to negotiate the state budget for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1. The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
